sections.content: Spanish uses ir a + infinitive to express a planned or imminent action. The simple future can also describe plans, especially when the speaker makes a prediction, promise or decision about what will happen. Travel plans often combine both forms: one can state an organised intention with ir a and then predict what the journey will involve.

items.spanish: Voy a preparar el itinerario esta noche.
items.english: I am going to prepare the itinerary tonight.

items.spanish: Mañana vamos a salir temprano para evitar el tráfico.
items.english: Tomorrow we are going to leave early to avoid the traffic.

items.spanish: El viaje será largo, pero llegaremos antes de anochecer.
items.english: The journey will be long, but we will arrive before nightfall.

items.spanish: Si todo está preparado, compraremos los billetes mañana.
items.english: If everything is ready, we will buy the tickets tomorrow.

sections.content: Use ir a + infinitive for an intention or plan that is already in view; use the future for predictions, promises and more neutral statements about what will happen.
